messages:
sam: FYI bringing up a new HF checkout (community-alpaca-ish, trimmed vocab) on Dedicated. Seeing streaming outputs cut off early when using our chat template + q8 quant. Looks like generation stops as soon as a duplicate EOS shows up in the token stream. Anyone seen this?

alice: Can you paste the exact small repro? model name, conversion steps, and which chat template you used.

sam: model id: local/community-alpaca-v2-trim. Conversion command: `transformers-cli convert --framework pt --model_name community-alpaca-v2 trimmed/` then `redwood model upload --path converted/ --quant q8`. Chat template: our default chat_template_v2 with stop seq ["\", "\n\n"]. Quick test prompt: "User: Summarize the following..."

ben: hmm stop seq includes empty-string token? That stop list looks weird. Also q8 conversion sometimes collapses token ids if tokenizer config/eos mapping is inconsistent. Do you have the model's config.json and tokenizer.json from the converted artifact?

sam: attaching snippets: `config.json` has "eos_token_id": 50256, tokenizer.json has "special_tokens_map": {"eos_token": ""} but tokenizer.vocab maps "" to id 50253. So mismatch.

carol: aha — mismatch between tokenizer.vocab eos id and config.json eos id. Streaming runtime checks eos_token_id from config and also honors special tokens coming from tokenizer. If they disagree we sometimes emit the first seen eos and treat the later one as normal text -> double-eos appears in token stream and our stop logic considers the first occurrence as final but the tokenizer streaming join triggers a flush on the second, leading to an early chunk end.

maria: quick repro log: `STREAM CHUNK: tokens [110, 45, 50253, 50253, 10] -> text '...\n'` In the trace we can see two consecutive 50253s (""), but config expected 50256. After quantize-and-strip we lost the mapping for 50256.

alice: two short fixes: 1) during HF->Redwood conversion, reconcile tokenizer special tokens to match config.eos_token_id OR 2) prefer tokenizer's explicit special_tokens_map over config.eos_token_id when building the Redwood model manifest. Which one is less risky?

ben: prefer #1 (reconcile) for safety. Script suggestion: when converting, run this check: 
```
# reconcile eos
if tokenizer.eos_token is not None and config.eos_token_id != tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(tokenizer.eos_token):
    logger.warn('mismatch, patching config.eos_token_id to tokenizer mapping')
    config.eos_token_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(tokenizer.eos_token)
    config.save_pretrained(outdir)
```
carol: also add a small integration test in the conversion pipeline that runs a 64-token streaming generation and asserts no duplicate-eos artifacts and that stops are respected when chat template stop sequences are set. Keep the test cheap but deterministic (use seed + small dataset).

sam: for the immediate prod workaround we changed the chat template to use a unique stop marker `<|stream_end|>` and patched tokenizer special tokens to include it mapped to the same ID as config.eos_token_id. That removed early truncation for this model.

maria: related note — quantization pipeline (q8) used a post-processing step that rebuilt token-id maps from a trimmed vocab; that code took the largest id from the trimmed table as eos if none explicitly set. That explains why 50256 -> 50253 drifted. I'll open a PR to make that deterministic.

deploy-bot: model-upload community-alpaca-v2-trim completed (artifact: m-2076543210-v1).

alice: great. Follow-ups: carol add the conversion reconciliation check + unit test; maria open PR for quant post-process; ben add a short runbook note about "check eos ids when seeing streaming early stop". Sam, after PRs we can re-run conversion and then re-quant to confirm.

sam: thanks everyone — putting a short repro and the patch into the bring-up doc now. :thumbsup:
